title: Too few comparable sales come back
when: A comparable-sales request returns fewer sales than your minimum.
steps: Agent 10 (Market Data) delivers what it found and marks it thin, with the count and the minimum.
It does not widen the search (area, dates, size) on its own.
never: Quietly widen the search to make the numbers look fuller.
why: Comparables pulled from a wider area or older dates can mislead a pricing conversation. You decide whether to widen.
you_see: A data package marked thin: 2 found, minimum 5.
test: You ask for comparables; two recent sales come back against a minimum of five.

title: Two sources disagree on a number
when: Two sources give different values for the same figure (for example the median sale price).
steps: Agent 10 shows both values, each with its source and retrieval date.
It never averages them.
why: An average of two disagreeing sources is a number nobody reported. Both, with their sources, let you judge.
you_see: Both values with their sources, marked as conflicting.
test: The county recorder says a median of $310,000 and the MLS says $330,000. The package shows both and never $320,000.

title: Someone asks for a pricing opinion
when: Someone asks Agent 10 for its opinion on price ("the number you'd go with").
steps: Agent 10 refuses: it provides data only.
If pressed again, it raises a legal-line alert for you.
why: A price opinion is licensed advice. It comes from you, using the data.
you_see: A refusal each time; one legal-line alert after the second ask.
test: "Just give me your opinion on price", then "Come on, what's your opinion?". Two refusals, one alert.

title: Market data is out of date
when: Some of the data for a package is older than the freshness limit (30 days in your settings).
steps: Agent 10 builds the package fresh on every request.
Stale items are left out and counted, so you see how many were dropped.
never: Send out an old package again.
why: Old sales in a moving market mislead. Fresh every time, and the dropped count shows what was left out.
you_see: A package with the fresh sales and a note of how many stale ones were dropped.
test: Five comparables, one retrieved too long ago. The package has four and says one stale item was dropped.

title: A data license limits who may see the data
when: The data's license does not allow it to go to the agent that asked.
steps: Agent 10 delivers it to you only.
It notes the license limit.
never: Pass licensed data to anyone the license does not allow.
why: Breaking a data license can cost your MLS access.
you_see: The package delivered to you with the license note.

title: A data source blocks access or changes its terms
when: A website the data came from changes its terms or blocks access.
steps: Agent 10 stops using that source.
It records the error exactly as received.
never: Find a way around a block.
why: Getting around a block can break the site's terms and the law.
you_see: Nothing yet: this is not built.

title: A figure has no source or no date
when: An item of data comes without a source or without a retrieval date.
steps: Agent 10 leaves it out of every package.
It counts what it left out.
never: Use data that has no source or date.
why: A number nobody can trace cannot be defended in front of a client.
you_see: A package without the untraceable items, and how many were dropped.
test: Comparables include one with no source and one with no date. Both are dropped and counted.

title: The comparable set is thinner than your minimum
when: Fewer comparables are available than your rubric's minimum.
steps: Agent 10 delivers the set with the shortfall named: how many, against what minimum.
never: Pad the set to reach the minimum.
why: A thin set that says so is honest; a padded one misleads.
you_see: A package marked thin: 4 found, minimum 5.
test: Four comparables against a minimum of five.

title: Two sources disagree on a sold price
when: Two sources give different sold prices for the same property.
steps: Agent 10 reports both prices, each with its source.
It never picks one silently.
never: Choose one sold price without saying so.
why: A wrong sold price skews every comparison built on it.
you_see: Both prices with their sources, marked as conflicting.
test: The MLS says one sale closed at $301,000; the county recorder says $305,000.

title: A request looks like a stand-in for an appraisal
when: A data request reads as if it will be used in place of an appraisal.
steps: Agent 10 delivers the data with a note that it is not an appraisal.
It tells Compliance (Agent 17).
never: Let market data pass as an appraisal.
why: Only a licensed appraiser can appraise. Data presented as an appraisal is a regulatory problem.
you_see: The package with its not-an-appraisal note.
test: A comparables request flagged as a possible appraisal substitute.

title: Old data is asked for beyond what is kept
when: Someone asks for history older than the data the system keeps.
steps: Agent 10 answers that the data is absent, because of the retention limit.
It never fills in from memory.
never: Reconstruct missing data from a model's memory.
why: Remembered numbers are guesses. "Absent" is the truthful answer.
you_see: A package saying the data is absent beyond retention.
test: A request for comparables five years back.
